claims.text: Active-learning MLIPs trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations near fusion can accurately reproduce solid- and liquid-phase free-energy surfaces.
Such MLIPs can retain anharmonic vibrational contributions to free energy.
Such MLIPs can retain electron–vibration coupling contributions to free energy.
MLIPs can enable fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic calculations at a fraction of the cost of explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
Elemental metals such as Al and binary alloys such as Ni–Fe are suitable prototype systems for this fusion methodology.
The fusion methodology can be extended to CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloys.
Training on solid and liquid configurations from approximately 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm is sufficient to construct the proposed near-fusion MLIP.
Active learning can automatically select configurations and generate training sets tailored to a specified class of systems and properties.
Active learning can reduce the amount of DFT training data required while retaining DFT-level or near-DFT accuracy.
The MLIP energy landscape will preserve local vibrational modes, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling characteristics.
Capturing the essential free-energy landscape with active learning bypasses full AIMD while maintaining the fidelity of vibrational and electronic contributions.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to both explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD.
MLIP predictions of phase free energies, latent heat, melting pressure, and related observables will agree with AIMD or TOR-TILD benchmarks within approximately 5–10%.
Explicit AIMD free-energy evaluations and TOR-TILD are highly accurate.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD are computationally prohibitive, particularly for multicomponent systems.
The expected validity range of the method is approximately 0.8Tm to 1.2Tm.
